lead: Tesla / TSLA — the inventor of our age is on sale
smaller: Bitcoin / BTC — the strategic reserve is coming
Leveraged ETFs / TQQQ and SOXL — three times the index, one day at a time
AST SpaceMobile / ASTS — the Starlink rival for phones
why_lead: Tesla has fallen 28.84% over 20 sessions, from 392.21 to 279.10, in a name that dominates retail coverage, and the attention is concrete on this date: Korean leveraged-ETF buyers were burned on the dip, a Morgan Stanley $430 target and Cathie Wood’s praise keep the bull story alive, and protests and an insider sale are in the news. The price drawdown and the crowd’s buy-the-dip reaction coincide, so the lead is the dip rather than a surge.
why_smaller: Bitcoin is the policy trade with the most retail-facing headlines on this date: a 6% pop on reserve hints, a 9% reversal earlier in the week, a $78K retest in play, and crypto ETF flows that swing by billions.
Leveraged ETFs are where the Tesla dip-buying turns into an instrument: SOXL is down 16.51% over five sessions, and zero-day options trading hit a record, which gives the list a non-equity trade.

AST SpaceMobile is the clearest surge in the card (up 18.14% in the prior session and 46.38% over 20 sessions), carried by one explainable story: a Starlink rival built for ordinary phones, with a Vodafone deal behind it.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir (PLTR): heavy attention and a 6.79% surge in the prior session, but the 20-session move (-13.19%) and the mixed fan sentiment were thinner than Tesla’s evidence; used in the sector and catalyst context instead.
Nebius (NBIS): a retail-elated item on a new 300 MW data-centre site, but the prior-session move was only 1.89% and the attention rests on one retail headline.
Rheinmetall (RHM.DE): the largest move among big names (up 60.59% over 20 sessions), but the attention is institutional and sector-level, so it sits in the sector and anticipatory sections.
Quantum names (IONQ, RGTI): deep 20-session drawdowns, but the evidence is commentary rather than dated retail-dip evidence.
MongoDB (MDB): a weak-guidance headline that conflicts with the card’s +3.83% prior-session move, so excluded.
Sandisk (SNDK): relisted-stock retail excitement, but the 20-session return is unavailable (14 prior observations), so there is no price evidence to pair with the attention.
CoreWeave: IPO filing and founder cash-out headlines, but no listed ticker in the card.
Memecoins: the 56% crash from the December peak has no card series behind it.
Gold and silver: small moves (gold up 1.75% over 20 sessions) and ordinary attention; the crypto reserve trade was the stronger policy story.
